finding.expected: Reconciliation must never claim a later matching RUN solely because it appeared after the pre-invocation namespace snapshot. A RUN may be reconciled only when durable state proves that the exact correction dispatch owns that RUN; otherwise the re-delivery remains non-executing and explicitly blocked/in-progress. Add regression coverage for both sides of the boundary: a crash before any dispatch-owned RUN binding followed by an unrelated matching RUN must not be attributed, while a crash after durable binding of the exact admitted REMEDIATION RUN may reconcile that bound RUN without re-execution.
finding.issue: Crash reconciliation can attribute an unrelated later REMEDIATION RUN to the correction dispatch using only temporal namespace delta plus matching task/review/ finding/executor metadata. If the A6 invocation crashes before creating or durably binding a RUN, another direct/manual execution of the same canonical remediation can create one matching RUN afterward; the current reconciler then treats that RUN as the unique continuation of the crashed dispatch even though no dispatch-owned binding proves causality. The added restart regression demonstrates this exact behavior by crashing before any RUN is created, writing a matching RUN afterward, and expecting it to be attributed. This violates the requirement that restart reconciliation bind only a uniquely attributable REMEDIATION RUN that can be proven to belong to the original correction delivery.
